requirements.evidence: All contract classes are present with the required signatures: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:16), UpdateQueue with nullable named params (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:15-21), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:16), enum with only `Call = 'call'`, QueueAccess model with array cast and membership()/queue() relations, a same-entity factory, and a migration with cascading FKs and unique (entity_membership_id, queue_id). Policy call() denies non-array permissions (QueuePolicy.php:498). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check (CallNextTicket.php:33). Ticket::call() follows the required order: lock queue, inactive check, authorize, then the waiting check (Ticket.php:413-435). Revoke only logs when a row was deleted (SetQueueAccess.php:174-182). Gaps: a name that slugifies to '' (e.g. '!!!') stores an empty slug (CreateQueue.php:70-74). An explicit slug that slugifies to '' is silently ignored on update instead of rejected (UpdateQueue.php:251-253). The race-condition detection misses PostgreSQL's 23505 / lower-case 'duplicate' message (CreateQueue.php:103-110). Other docs were updated, but the database-schema.md edit only changes the status line.

conventions.evidence: Writes go through Actions, authorization lives in QueuePolicy via Gate::forUser()->authorize, the model uses #[Fillable] like its siblings, the migration has a reversible down(), and CHANGELOG plus both docs are updated. However, the TDD convention ('No production code without a test; everything implemented ships with a test') is broken: there are no tests for CreateQueue, UpdateQueue, SetQueueAccess, QueuePolicy, the QueueAccess factory or the new Ticket::call() authorization.

security.evidence: Every new action authorizes first (CreateQueue.php:60, UpdateQueue.php:232, SetQueueAccess.php:136), so nothing is written for unauthorized users. Both call paths now enforce the `call` ability. The cross-entity membership/queue check is present (SetQueueAccess.php:138). Permissions are validated against the enum, and mass assignment is restricted. Small concern: isUniqueViolation treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (including FK/NOT NULL violations) as a duplicate slug, which hides other integrity errors as validation errors. The correctness of the policy depends on User::membershipFor and App\Models\UserRole, which are not shown in the diff.

tests.evidence: The only test change is tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php, which adds owner memberships so existing tests keep passing (lines 629-733). There is no test for the new behavior: no unauthorized-caller test for CallNextTicket, nothing for CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess (slug uniqueness, validation, audit logs, revoke), nothing for the QueuePolicy employee-grant/corrupted-permissions cases, and nothing for the new Ticket::call() ordering. Existing Ticket::call() tests (not shown) may also need memberships.

simplicity.evidence: The code is generally direct, but isUniqueViolation() is copy-pasted between CreateQueue.php:101-111 and UpdateQueue.php:299-309, and the name-validation block is duplicated (CreateQueue.php:64-68 / UpdateQueue.php:239-243). The DB::transaction around a single save (UpdateQueue.php:282-285) adds nothing. QueueAccessFactory eagerly creates an Entity inside definition() even when its attributes are overridden (QueueAccessFactory.php:542).

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are short and the flow is linear. The Ticket::call() PHPDoc was updated (Ticket.php:401-402). Nits: the policy hard-codes 'call' instead of QueuePermission::Call->value (QueuePolicy.php:502), and `protected $table` is placed before `use HasFactory` (QueueAccess.php:344-347).

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the task: actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, call-path enforcement, docs, changelog and the test fixtures adjusted for the new authorization. There is no delete action, no UI and no unrelated refactor.

issues.explanation: No tests cover the new actions, the QueuePolicy, the audit logging or the unauthorized/inactive paths in CallNextTicket and Ticket::call(), which violates the project's mandatory TDD convention.
If the name slugifies to an empty string (e.g. only punctuation), an empty slug is persisted instead of being rejected as invalid.
An explicit slug that slugifies to '' is silently replaced by the current slug instead of raising a ValidationException.
Unique-violation detection treats every SQLSTATE 23000 integrity error as a duplicate slug and misses PostgreSQL's 23505 and its lower-case 'duplicate key' message.
isUniqueViolation() and the name validation are duplicated verbatim from CreateQueue instead of being shared.
Wrapping a single save() in DB::transaction adds no atomicity.
Uses the literal 'call' instead of QueuePermission::Call->value.
Entity::factory()->create() runs inside definition(), so an entity is created even when the caller overrides membership and queue.

review.summary: The change adds the CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess actions, the QueueAccess model and migration, the QueuePermission enum and the QueuePolicy, and enforces the `call` ability in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call() in the required order. The implementation follows the contract closely, apart from small slug edge cases and duplicated helpers. However, it ships no tests for any of the new behavior, which breaks the project's mandatory TDD convention, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
